{{Short description|Taiwanese chemist, politician, and diplomat (1936–2019)}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Mao (surname)|Mao]]|lang=Chinese}}
[[File:毛高文.jpg|thumb|Mao Kao-wen]]
'''Mao Kao-wen''' ({{zh|t=毛高文|p=Máo Gāowén}}; 9 February 1936 [[Fenghua]], [[Ningbo]] – 28 October 2019 [[Taipei]]) was a Taiwanese [[chemist]], politician, and diplomat. He served as the president of [[National Tsinghua University]] from 1981 to 1987. He also was the [[Ministry of Education (Taiwan)|Minister of Education]] of the [[Republic of China]] from June 1987 to February 1993.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.chinapost.com.tw/commentary/the-china-post/daniel-j.-bauer/2009/01/11/191505/p2/Good-humor.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120929220534/http://www.chinapost.com.tw/commentary/the-china-post/daniel-j.-bauer/2009/01/11/191505/p2/Good-humor.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 29, 2012|title=Good humor and old proverbs|date=11 January 2009|work=[[The China Post]]|accessdate=27 April 2011}}</ref>

Mao died on 28 October 2019 at the [[Taipei Veterans General Hospital]], aged 83.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cckf.org/en/news/2019110804|title=Professor Kao-wen Mao, Former Chairman of the Foundation, has Passed Away|date=2019-10-29|work=Chiang Ching Kuo Foundation|access-date=2019-12-07}}</ref>
